chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Seeing Sidney Bechet in Jimmy Cooper's show
summary: Going alone as a loner, he heard Bechet's soprano solo in a burlesque show and comments that the saxophone then had no standard sound.

venues.name: Jimmy Cooper's Black and White Show

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: When Sidney Bechet came up to Boston with that show, I imagine you all went to hear him.
No, I went there by myself.
You went there by yourself.
Well, see, I'll tell you. I've been a loner practically all my life. I didn't hang out with gangs or this, that and the other. And when I went anyplace,
Holmes (10/9) - 31

usually I went by myself. Well, shows... I wasn't used to going to shows anyway. That was big-time stuff. And I was not a big-timer. Of course, when there was something special going on at a show, then I would make up my mind to go -- I would go by myself. I didn't ask anybody else. Because I didn't have anybody else's fare to pay!
Tell me about Bechet coming to Boston.

Well, it was no big deal to me. He was just in the show. He was just another performer. Got up and played a solo. And as far I knew... I had never even heard of Bechet before. He played this... It was so... He surprised me so much when he stood up and played a solo... I didn't know who he was, but he sure was playing. Then I found out afterwards that he was Sidney Bechet. Well, who was Sidney Bechet? You know.
Well, this was the first time you saw a straight soprano?
Yes.
The first time you heard a straight...
Mmm...yeah.
At least played the way Bechet...
Yeah.
Did it impress you?
Oh, yes. He impressed me very much. I
Holmes (10/9) - 32

liked it. I liked it very much. I never heard a saxophone played like that. Well, I'll tell you, I hadn't heard saxophone played many different ways anyway. The fact is, at that time, saxophone wasn't even regarded as an instrument. It was not regarded as an instrument. There was no set tone for it, how it's supposed to sound. You know, anybody's guess was as good as the other one. That's why at that time you had so many different kind of sounds on the saxophone. There was slap-tonguing, and this-that-and-the-other, and oh, a bunch of everything. And one was as good as the other. There was no right way.
And the show that Sidney Bechet was in?
It was a burlesque show. Jimmy Cooper's Black and White Show.
